```javascript
'use strict';

// `memo clear`: dry run by default, honest deletion, tombstones that survive a sweep.

const test = require('node:test');
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const fs = require('node:fs');
const os = require('node:os');
const path = require('node:path');
const { execFileSync, spawnSync } = require('node:child_process');

const MEMO = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'bin', 'memo.js');
const HAS_GIT = !spawnSync('git', ['--version'], { windowsHide: true }).error;
const SKIP = !HAS_GIT && 'git not installed';

const SID_A = 'aaaaaaaa-1111-4222-8333-444444444444';
const SID_B = 'bbbbbbbb-1111-4222-8333-444444444444';
const DATE = '2026-10-21';

function eventsFor(sid, prefix) {
  const at = (n) => '2026-10-21T09:0' + n + ':00.000+05:30';
  return [1, 2, 3].map((seq) => ({
    v: 1, id: 'e-' + prefix + '000' + seq, sid, seq, ts: at(seq), agent: 'claude-code',
    type: seq === 1 ? 'user_prompt' : 'assistant_text', text: 'event ' + seq + ' of ' + prefix
  }));
}

function recordLine(over) {
  return {
    op: 'create', id: over.id, type: over.type, ts: '2026-10-21T09:10:00.000+05:30', job: 'j-test',
    statement: over.statement, status: over.status || 'active', confidence: 'medium',
    evidence: over.evidence, sessions: over.sessions, source: 'llm'
  };
}

function setup(t) {
  const base = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'memo-clear-test-'));
  const root = path.join(base, 'repo');
  const home = path.join(base, 'home');
  fs.mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
  fs.mkdirSync(home, { recursive: true });
  t.after(() => fs.rmSync(base, { recursive: true, force: true }));

  const gitConfig = path.join(base, 'gitconfig');
  fs.writeFileSync(gitConfig, '[user]\n\tname = MEMO Test\n\temail = memo@test.invalid\n[commit]\n\tgpgsign = false\n');
  const env = {
    ...process.env, MEMO_HOME: home, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: gitConfig, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
    MEMO_CLAUDE_SETTINGS: path.join(base, 'claude.json')
  };
  delete env.MEMO_MOCK_LLM;
  execFileSync('git', ['init', '-q'], { cwd: root, windowsHide: true, env });

  const memo = (args) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [MEMO, ...args], {
    cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', windowsHide: true, env
  });
  assert.equal(memo(['init']).status, 0);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(home, 'config.json'),
    JSON.stringify({ v: 1, provider: 'mock', model: 'claude-haiku-5-5' }, null, 2) + '\n');

  const dir = path.join(root, '.memory', 'sessions', '2026', '10', '21');
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  const index = [];
  for (const [sid, prefix] of [[SID_A, 'aaaa'], [SID_B, 'bbbb']]) {
    const list = eventsFor(sid, prefix);
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, sid + '.jsonl'), list.map((e) => JSON.stringify(e)).join('\n') + '\n');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, sid + '.md'), '# Session ' + sid.slice(0, 8) + '\n\nsummary text\n');
    index.push({
      sid, agent: 'claude-code', date: DATE, start: list[0].ts, end: list[2].ts,
      events: 3, processedThrough: 3, summary: 'did things in ' + prefix, status: 'ended'
    });
  }
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, '.memory', 'sessions', 'index.json'), JSON.stringify(index, null, 2) + '\n');

  const records = path.join(root, '.memory', 'records');
  fs.mkdirSync(records, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(records, 'decisions.jsonl'),
    JSON.stringify(recordLine({
      id: 'D-only0001', type: 'decision', statement: 'only from session A',
      evidence: ['e-aaaa0001'], sessions: [SID_A]
    })) + '\n' +
    JSON.stringify(recordLine({
      id: 'D-mixed001', type: 'decision', statement: 'from both sessions',
      evidence: ['e-aaaa0002', 'e-bbbb0002'], sessions: [SID_A, SID_B]
    })) + '\n' +
    JSON.stringify(recordLine({
      id: 'D-other001', type: 'decision', statement: 'only from session B',
      evidence: ['e-bbbb0003'], sessions: [SID_B]
    })) + '\n');

  // Pretend capture has a cursor for session A, as it would after a live session.
  const repoId = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(home, 'repos.json'), 'utf8'))[0].id;
  const stateDir = path.join(home, 'state', repoId);
  fs.mkdirSync(stateDir, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(stateDir, 'cursors.json'), JSON.stringify({
    [SID_A]: { transcriptPath: path.join(base, 'transcript-a.jsonl').replace(/\\/g, '/'), offset: 0, lineNo: 0, tools: {} }
  }, null, 2));
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(base, 'transcript-a.jsonl'),
    JSON.stringify({ type: 'user', uuid: 'u1', message: { role: 'user', content: 'hello again' } }) + '\n');

  execFileSync('git', ['add', '-A'], { cwd: root, windowsHide: true, env });
  execFileSync('git', ['commit', '-q', '-m', 'base'], { cwd: root, windowsHide: true, env });

  return { base, root, home, env, memo, repoId, dir, stateDir };
}

function decisions(root) {
  const file = path.join(root, '.memory', 'records', 'decisions.jsonl');
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return [];
  return fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
}

function index(root) {
  return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, '.memory', 'sessions', 'index.json'), 'utf8'));
}

test('a dry run lists files and records and changes nothing', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  const r = ctx.memo(['clear', '--session', 'aaaaaaaa']);
  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /clear session aaaaaaaa/);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /\.memory\/sessions\/2026\/10\/21\/aaaaaaaa-1111-4222-8333-444444444444\.jsonl/);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /D-only0001/);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /D-mixed001/);
  assert.match(r.stdout, /dry run — nothing was deleted/);
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')));
  assert.equal(decisions(ctx.root).length, 3);
});

test('deleting a session removes its files, keeps the other, strips mixed evidence', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  const r = ctx.memo(['clear', '--session', SID_A, '--with-derived', '--yes']);
  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);

  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')), false);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.md')), false);
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_B + '.jsonl')), 'the other session stays');

  const left = decisions(ctx.root);
  assert.equal(left.find((d) => d.id === 'D-only0001'), undefined, 'derived-only record is gone');
  const mixed = left.find((d) => d.id === 'D-mixed001');
  assert.deepEqual(mixed.evidence, ['e-bbbb0002'], 'only the deleted session evidence is stripped');
  assert.deepEqual(mixed.sessions, [SID_B]);
  assert.equal(mixed.source_deleted, true);
  assert.ok(left.find((d) => d.id === 'D-other001'), 'untouched record stays untouched');

  const tomb = index(ctx.root).find((e) => e.sid === SID_A);
  assert.ok(tomb.deletedAt, 'a tombstone replaces the index entry');

  const state = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ctx.root, '.memory', 'PROJECT_STATE.md'), 'utf8');
  assert.equal(state.includes('only from session A'), false);
  assert.equal(state.includes(SID_A.slice(0, 8)), false);

  assert.match(r.stdout, /Older Git commits still contain this data/);
  const files = execFileSync('git', ['show', '--name-only', '--format=%s', 'HEAD'],
    { cwd: ctx.root, encoding: 'utf8', windowsHide: true }).trim().split('\n');
  assert.match(files[0], /^memo: remove captured session data for session aaaaaaaa$/);
  for (const f of files.slice(1).filter(Boolean)) assert.match(f, /^\.memory\//);
});

test('without --with-derived the derived record is kept but loses its evidence', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  const dry = ctx.memo(['clear', '--session', SID_A]);
  assert.match(dry.stdout, /add --with-derived to delete them too/);
  assert.equal(ctx.memo(['clear', '--session', SID_A, '--yes']).status, 0);
  const only = decisions(ctx.root).find((d) => d.id === 'D-only0001');
  assert.ok(only, 'the record survives');
  assert.deepEqual(only.evidence, []);
  assert.equal(only.source_deleted, true);
});

test('a tombstoned session is not re-imported by the next sweep', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  assert.equal(ctx.memo(['clear', '--session', SID_A, '--yes']).status, 0);
  const sweep = ctx.memo(['capture', '--sweep', '--verbose']);
  assert.equal(sweep.status, 0, sweep.stderr);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')), false, 'the session must stay deleted');
  const entry = index(ctx.root).find((e) => e.sid === SID_A);
  assert.ok(entry.deletedAt);
  assert.equal(entry.events, undefined);
});

test('a whole date needs --confirm and then removes every session of that day', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  const refused = ctx.memo(['clear', '--date', DATE, '--yes']);
  assert.equal(refused.status, 1);
  assert.match(refused.stderr, /needs --confirm 2026-10-21/);
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')));

  const r = ctx.memo(['clear', '--date', DATE, '--with-derived', '--yes', '--confirm', DATE]);
  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')), false);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_B + '.jsonl')), false);
  assert.equal(decisions(ctx.root).length, 0);
  assert.equal(index(ctx.root).every((e) => e.deletedAt), true);
});

test('one record can be deleted on its own', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  const r = ctx.memo(['clear', '--record', 'D-mixed001', '--yes']);
  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
  assert.deepEqual(decisions(ctx.root).map((d) => d.id).sort(), ['D-only0001', 'D-other001']);
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')), 'session files are untouched');
});

test('bad targets are refused without touching anything', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  for (const args of [
    ['clear', '--session', '../../etc/passwd', '--yes'],
    ['clear', '--session', 'zzzzzzzz', '--yes'],
    ['clear', '--date', '21-10-2026', '--yes'],
    ['clear', '--record', 'D-nope0000', '--yes'],
    ['clear', '--session', SID_A, '--date', DATE]
  ]) {
    const r = ctx.memo(args);
    assert.equal(r.status, 1, args.join(' ') + ' should fail');
  }
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')));
  assert.equal(decisions(ctx.root).length, 3);
});

test('--all-repo-data needs the typed phrase and keeps legacy notes', { skip: SKIP }, (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(ctx.root, '.memory', 'legacy'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(ctx.root, '.memory', 'legacy', 'decisions.md'), '# old\n');

  const refused = ctx.memo(['clear', '--all-repo-data', '--yes']);
  assert.equal(refused.status, 1);
  assert.match(refused.stderr, /DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA/);
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')));

  const r = ctx.memo(['clear', '--all-repo-data', '--yes', '--confirm', 'DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA']);
  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.dir, SID_A + '.jsonl')), false);
  assert.deepEqual(index(ctx.root), []);
  assert.equal(decisions(ctx.root).length, 0);
  assert.ok(fs.existsSync(path.join(ctx.root, '.memory', 'legacy', 'decisions.md')), 'legacy notes are kept');
```

```javascript
const os = require('node:os');
const path = require('node:path');

  t.after(() => fs.rmSync(base, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  const root = path.join(base, 'repo');
  const dir = path.join(root, '.memory', 'sessions', '2026', '10', '21');
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, SID_A + '.jsonl'),
    [1, 2, 3].map((seq) => JSON.stringify({
      v: 1, id: 'e-aaaa000' + seq, sid: SID_A, seq, ts: '2026-10-21T09:0' + seq + ':00.000+05:30',
      agent: 'claude-code', type: 'assistant_text', text: 'x'
    })).join('\n') + '\n');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, SID_A + '.md'), '# Session aaaaaaaa\n\nfixed the redact regex\n');
  const older = path.join(root, '.memory', 'sessions', '2026', '10', '20');
  fs.mkdirSync(older, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(older, SID_B + '.jsonl'), '');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, '.memory', 'sessions', 'index.json'), JSON.stringify([
    { sid: SID_A, agent: 'claude-code', date: '2026-10-21', start: '2026-10-21T09:01:00.000+05:30',
      end: '2026-10-21T09:03:00.000+05:30', events: 3, processedThrough: 3, summary: 'fixed the redact regex', status: 'ended' },
    { sid: SID_B, agent: 'claude-code', date: '2026-10-20', start: '2026-10-20T20:00:00.000+05:30',
      end: '2026-10-20T20:10:00.000+05:30', events: 5, processedThrough: 2, summary: '', status: 'ended' },
    { sid: 'cccccccc-1111-4222-8333-444444444444', agent: 'claude-code', date: '2026-10-19', deletedAt: '2026-10-21T10:00:00.000+05:30' }
  ], null, 2) + '\n');

  const records = path.join(root, '.memory', 'records');
  fs.mkdirSync(records, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(records, 'tasks.jsonl'),
    JSON.stringify({ op: 'create', id: 'T-11112222', type: 'task', ts: '2026-10-21T09:10:00.000+05:30',
      title: 'write the installer', status: 'open', priority: 'high', effort_estimate: '1-2h',
      capability: 'medium', evidence: ['e-aaaa0001'], sessions: [SID_A] }) + '\n' +
    JSON.stringify({ op: 'create', id: 'T-33334444', type: 'task', ts: '2026-10-21T09:11:00.000+05:30',
      title: 'ship it', status: 'done', evidence: ['e-aaaa0002'], sessions: [SID_A] }) + '\n');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(records, 'decisions.jsonl'),
    JSON.stringify({ op: 'create', id: 'D-aaaa1111', type: 'decision', ts: '2026-10-21T09:12:00.000+05:30',
      statement: 'ship a VBS launcher', status: 'active', evidence: ['e-aaaa0003'], sessions: [SID_A] }) + '\n');
  return { root };
}

test('the main menu lists every entry and flags a paused install', () => {
  const text = menu.renderMenu({ paused: false }, 'C:/code/my-repo');
  for (const [key, label] of menu.ITEMS) assert.match(text, new RegExp('\\s' + key + '\\s+' + label));
  assert.match(text, /my-repo/);
  assert.equal(/PAUSED/.test(text), false);
  assert.match(menu.renderMenu({ paused: true }, 'C:/code/my-repo'), /\[PAUSED\]/);
  assert.ok(text.trimEnd().split('\n').length <= 25);
});

test('the clear screen warns before anything is typed', () => {
  const text = menu.renderClearMenu();
  assert.match(text, /dry run first/);
  assert.match(text, /type DELETE/);
  assert.match(text, /Older Git commits still contain this data/);
  assert.match(menu.renderPurgeNote(), /git filter-repo/);
  assert.ok(text.trimEnd().split('\n').length <= 25);
});

test('browse by date lists dates newest first, without deleted sessions', (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);

  const dates = text.match(/2026-10-\d\d/g);
  assert.deepEqual(dates, ['2026-10-21', '2026-10-20']);
  assert.match(text, /2026-10-21 {3}\s*1 session\(s\) · {4}3 events/);
});

  assert.equal(/bbbbbbbb/.test(text), false, 'the other date is not listed');

});

test('show prints the summary, the file paths and the records of one session', (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  const text = browse.renderShow(ctx.root, 'aaaaaaaa');
  assert.match(text, /events file {2}\.memory\/sessions\/2026\/10\/21\/aaaaaaaa/);
  assert.match(text, /summary file \.memory\/sessions\/2026\/10\/21\/aaaaaaaa-1111-4222-8333-444444444444\.md/);
  assert.match(text, /fixed the redact regex/);
  assert.match(text, /T-11112222 task/);
  assert.match(text, /D-aaaa1111 decision/);
});

test('show refuses an unknown or ambiguous id instead of guessing', (t) => {
  const ctx = setup(t);
  assert.match(browse.renderShow(ctx.root, 'zzzz'), /no session matches zzzz/);

});

test('tasks shows open work by default and everything with --all', (t) => {

  assert.equal(/T-33334444/.test(open), false);
  assert.match(browse.renderTasks(ctx.root, { all: true }), /T-33334444/);
});
```

````markdown
# Security and privacy

What MEMO reads, what leaves your machine, and what you can delete.
Short version: MEMO is a local tool that writes Markdown and JSONL into your repo,
and sends batches of captured events to one API provider you configure.

## 1. What is captured

Capture only happens in a repo where you ran `memo init` (the repo is then listed in
`~/.memo/repos.json`). Claude Code calls `memo capture` on SessionStart, Stop, PreCompact
and SessionEnd; MEMO reads the new bytes of that session's transcript file.

Kept (`src/capture/claude.js`, limits from the plan §6.1):

| Event | What is stored | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `user_prompt` | your prompt text | 4,000 chars |
| `assistant_text` | the reply text | 3,000 chars |
| `tool_call` | tool name + the Bash command or the file path | 300 chars |
| `tool_result` | first 500 + last 300 chars, plus `ok: true/false` | 800 chars |
| `system`, `git_commit` | short marker lines | — |

Dropped before anything is written to disk:

- thinking blocks
- `Read` results (only the `tool_call` with the path is kept)
- `Write` / `Edit` content (path and line counts only)
- image blocks
- anything whose path matches `config.denyPaths`
  (default `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `credentials*.json`, `secrets/**`)

File paths are stored relative to the repo root. A path outside the repo becomes
`<outside-repo>`; your home directory is never written into the event text.

## 2. Redaction

`src/redact.js` runs twice: once when the event is written to disk, once again when the
prompt is built in `src/extract/prompt.js`. It removes API keys (`sk-ant-…`, `sk-proj-…`,
`AKIA…`, bearer tokens), credentials inside connection strings, `.env`-style
`NAME=value` lines and long high-entropy strings next to the words key/secret/token.

**Redaction is regex-based. It is a safety net, not a guarantee.** Read `.memory/` once
before you push a repo somewhere public. If a secret did land in a file, rotate the secret —
removing it from the current file does not remove it from older commits.

## 3. What is sent to the API

`memo process` (directly or from `memo cycle`) sends, per call:

- the fixed system prompt
- the repo folder name (not its full path)
- up to 60 open records (id, type, status, statement)
- one batch of event envelopes, capped at `maxInputTokensPerCall` (default 12,000 tokens)

Nothing else is uploaded: no file contents, no git remote, no username, no machine name.
Provider and model come from `~/.memo/config.json`. With `provider: "mock"` no network
call happens at all. With `apiEnabled: false` or `memo pause`, no call happens either.

Your provider's own retention and training policy applies to what you send — check it
and record the link in `docs/PHASE0_FINDINGS.md` §6 before using a real key.

## 4. Where data lives

| Location | Contents | In Git? |
|---|---|---|
| `.memory/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<sid>.jsonl` | captured events | yes |
| `.memory/sessions/<sid>.md`, `index.json` | summaries, session index + tombstones | yes |
| `.memory/records/*.jsonl` | decisions, errors, tasks, learnings, facts, questions, intent | yes |
| `.memory/PROJECT_STATE.md`, `TASKS.md`, `progress.md` | generated reports | yes |
| `~/.memo/config.json`, `repos.json`, `state/`, `logs/` | machine state, cursors, jobs, usage | never |
| `~/.memo/personal.md` | your personal notes | never |

`memo commit` only ever stages `.memory/` (`git commit --only -- .memory`), never your
source files, and never pushes.

## 5. The API key

The key is read from the environment variable named by `config.apiKeyEnv`
(default `MEMO_API_KEY`, falling back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
It is never written into a config file, never logged, and only ever displayed as
`set (…last4)`.

`install_memo.bat` stores it with `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(…, 'User')`
after reading it with `Read-Host -AsSecureString`, so it is not echoed and not kept in
your shell history. It is still a plain user environment variable, readable by anything
running as you. DPAPI encryption is planned for P11.

## 6. Deleting data

```
memo clear --session <sid>                 # dry run: files, sizes, affected records
memo clear --session <sid> --with-derived --yes
memo clear --date 2026-10-21 --yes --confirm 2026-10-21
memo clear --record T-1b2c3d4e --yes
memo clear --all-repo-data --yes --confirm DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA
```

A deleted session gets a tombstone in `index.json`, so the next capture sweep does not
re-import it from the Claude transcript. The deletion itself is committed.

**Honest limit:** this removes the data from the current files only. Older Git commits
still contain it, and copies on GitHub or in other clones are unaffected. Full erasure
needs history rewriting (`git filter-repo` + force push), which MEMO does not do for you.

## 7. Turning it off

- `memo pause` — the scheduled task keeps running but does nothing
- `memo setup claude --remove` — removes the Claude Code hooks (a backup of
  `~/.claude/settings.json` is written first)
- `scripts\windows\uninstall_memo.bat` — removes the task, the logon entry and the hooks;
  it never deletes `.memory/` or `~/.memo` unless you type `DELETE-ALL-MEMO-DATA`

## 8. Trust boundaries

- The model's output is validated by `src/extract/validate.js` before anything is written:
  unknown fields are dropped, enums are enforced, `files` must be relative with no `..`.
  Model output is never executed, never used as a path outside `.memory/`, and never
  changes the config.
- `verified` / `done` are only accepted with a passing `tool_result` as evidence,
  otherwise they are downgraded and marked `downgraded: true`.
- Hooks and the scheduled task catch every error, log to `~/.memo/logs/` and exit 0,
  so a MEMO bug cannot fail your Claude Code session or your commit.
````

```markdown
# Supported agents

MEMO captures one agent today: **Claude Code**. Everything else is either planned or
out of scope. Fill the "verified on" rows during the P6 end-to-end run.

## Claude Code

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Capture method | hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` → `memo capture` reads the session transcript |
| Hook events used | `SessionStart` (also prints the project context), `Stop`, `PreCompact`, `SessionEnd` |
| Transcript format | JSONL, one message per line, read incrementally by byte offset |
| Installed by | `memo setup claude` (backs the settings file up first, idempotent) |
| Removed by | `memo setup claude --remove` |
| Version verified | _fill in: `claude --version` output used for the P6 run_ |
| Terminal (PowerShell) | _fill in: pass / fail_ |
| Terminal (Git Bash) | _fill in: pass / fail_ |
| VS Code extension | _fill in: pass / fail_ |

### How it works

1. A session starts → `SessionStart` fires → MEMO records the transcript path in
   `~/.memo/state/<repoId>/cursors.json` and prints `memo context` to stdout, which
   Claude Code adds to the session context.
2. Each turn end (`Stop`), each compaction (`PreCompact`) and the session end
   (`SessionEnd`) fire → MEMO reads only the bytes after the stored offset, normalizes
   them into event envelopes, redacts them and appends to
   `.memory/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<sid>.jsonl`.
3. Every 15 minutes `memo cycle` sweeps anything the hooks missed, extracts records and
   commits `.memory/`.

### Known limits

- **Two sessions in the same repo at once** — both are captured, but their events
  interleave in separate files; cross-session consolidation is P7/P8 work.
- **Resumed or forked sessions** reuse the same session id: capture continues from the
  stored offset, so a fork may be recorded under the parent id.
- **Compaction rewrite** — if Claude Code rewrites the transcript file shorter than the
  stored offset, MEMO logs `transcript_rewritten`, resets the offset to 0 and re-reads;
  event ids make the re-read idempotent.
- **Subagent transcripts** are not captured (P8).
- **Worktrees and branch switches** — the repo root is resolved per hook call; a second
  worktree of the same repo is a separate root and needs its own `memo init`.
- **Transcript retention** — if Claude Code deletes old transcripts
  (`cleanupPeriodDays`) before a sweep runs, those events are lost; the hooks normally
  capture them long before that.
- **Hook failures are silent by design**: `memo capture` always exits 0 and logs to
  `~/.memo/logs/capture.jsonl`, so a MEMO problem never breaks your session.

## Not supported yet

| Agent | Status |
|---|---|
| Codex CLI | planned, P9 — needs an adapter in `src/capture/codex.js` |
| Cursor / Windsurf / Copilot Chat | no stable local transcript + hook contract checked yet |
| Plain `git` usage without an agent | partially: the post-commit hook writes `.memory/progress.md` |

## Adding another agent

1. Write `src/capture/<agent>.js` with a `normalize(line, ctx) → envelope[]` function
   that produces the §6.1 envelope (`type`, `id`, `seq`, `ts`, `agent`, `text`, `ok`).
2. Reuse `src/capture/capture.js` for cursors, locking, dedup and session files.
3. Add redacted fixture transcripts under `test/fixtures/<agent>/` and a
   `test/capture-<agent>.test.js` that runs offline.
4. Add the install path (hooks, wrapper or polling) and document it here.

```

```text
# MEMO

MEMO is a zero-dependency Node.js CLI that gives a Git repo a persistent memory for AI coding agents.

## Where memory lives
- `.memory/` (tracked): project memory — progress log, decisions, errors, next steps, and later `PROJECT_STATE.md`.
- `~/.memo/` (per machine, never in Git): personal notes, logs, local state.

## Before starting work
- Read `.memory/PROJECT_STATE.md` if it exists (`memo report` regenerates it).
- If it does not exist, read `.memory/progress.md`.

## Code map
- `bin/memo.js` — CLI entry (`init | note | hook | report | context | commit | migrate | setup claude | capture | config | process`).
- `src/` — implementation (paths, git, init, note, hook, brief, redact, config, usage).
- `src/capture/`, `src/store/` — Claude Code capture and the session/record files.
- `src/llm/`, `src/extract/` — provider clients and `memo process` extraction (see `docs/PHASE2_API_EXTRACTION.md`).
- `src/report/`, `src/context.js` — `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `TASKS.md`, and the SessionStart context.
- `src/gitops/memory-commit.js`, `src/migrate.js` — `.memory/`-only commits and legacy-note import.
- `templates/` — post-commit hook, AGENTS block, CLAUDE.md and `.memory/README.md` written by `memo init`.
- `test/` — `node:test` suites; run `npm test`.
=== block template ===
<!-- memo:start -->
## Project memory (MEMO)
- Current state: `.memory/PROJECT_STATE.md` (open tasks, errors, decisions, recent sessions). Read it before starting work.
- Task list: `.memory/TASKS.md`. How the folder works: `.memory/README.md`.
- These files are generated; corrections go through `memo note -t <decision|error|next> "text"`.
<!-- memo:end -->
```

## Jo banaya (P4 / P5 / P6)

**P4 — worker + installer + status**
| File | Kya karta hai |
|---|---|

| `src/status.js` | `memo status` (≤20 lines), `memo doctor` (11 checks, har FAIL pe fix hint, `--live` = ek API ping), `memo pause/resume` |
| `src/install.js` | `memo install`: config, Claude hooks, privacy notice, provider/model prompt |
| `scripts/windows/` | `install_memo.bat`, `uninstall_memo.bat`, `memo_status.bat`, `memo_console.bat`, `register-task.ps1`, `run-hidden.vbs` — sab CRLF |

Key 'Read-Host -AsSecureString' se leta hai, kabhi echo nahi hota; task `MultipleInstances IgnoreNew` + `StartWhenAvailable` + 10-min limit, dobara chalane pe update hota hai, duplicate nahi.

**P5 — browse + clear**
`src/delete.js` (plan/apply, dry-run default), `src/browse.js` (`sessions`/`show`/`tasks`), `src/ui/menu.js` (`memo console`, 1–6/0).
Deleted session ka tombstone `index.json` mein jata hai → agla sweep use wapas import nahi karta (test se verify). Mixed-source records rakhe jate hain, sirf target evidence strip hota hai + `source_deleted:true`. Commit message: `memo: remove captured session data for <scope>`, aur har baar honest note: purane Git commits mein data abhi bhi hai.

**P6 — docs**
`docs/SECURITY.md`, `docs/SUPPORTED_AGENTS.md`, `PHASE0_FINDINGS.md` mein §10 Measurements + §11 E2E checklist.

Purane modules mein 3 chhote badlav: `capture.js` (sweepRepo + tombstone skip), `report/state.js` (tombstones report nahi hote), `memory-commit.js` (custom message option).
